newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ to use forex swaps in liquidity management.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ to use forex swaps in liquidity management.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Tuesday it planned to start using foreign exchange swaps in about six weeks as another tool to help smooth liquidity flows.
At a briefing, a spokesman for the bank said he did not expect the move to have any impact on monetary policy or on the New Zealand dollar.
The bank said it had been reviewing its instruments in the light of two recent developments.
The first was the elimination of the government's net foreign debt, which had significantly reduced the amount of foreign exchange business the Reserve Bank did.
The other was projected large budget surpluses, which had made the bank review how monetary policy might be run effectively in an environment where government securities played a smaller role.
Switzerland also uses forex swaps as a form of liquidity management.

The spokesman said one reason for using the new system was that the New Zealand foreign exchange market was one of the deepest and most liquid of New Zealand markets. Daily turnover is around US$8 billion daily, with some $6 billion of that transacted in the forwards market.
He said what will motivate the bank to use the swaps market rather than the repo market will be which one offers the better return.
He said with the elimination of net foreign debt, the bank's staff needed to maintain contacts and skills in the foreign exchange market and use of swaps would help them to do so.

Entry into the swaps market will be conducted potentially at any time of the day, the spokesman said, and the bank at this stage would not reveal its operations. However, he stressed operations would be on a relatively small scale.
